Hey Elliot — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the friction. Calendly/Chili Piper sometimes default to the browser locale or an account-level timezone which creates this exact confusion across IST/CET/PDT.

Short answer: yes — we can avoid the scheduler widget entirely and I can send a single-ICS invite using UTC as the canonical time. That avoids browser-local conversion bugs.

Proposed workflow (two quick options):
1) I send an ICS with 3 candidate slots expressed in UTC (and local equivalents in the body). You pick one and accept — calendar systems will convert consistently.
2) If you prefer the widget, use this Chili Piper link with "force_tz=UTC" param I can append, or change your Calendly display timezone (Calendly > Account Settings > Timezone) — but that doesn't always solve cross-tenant issues.

Candidate windows (UTC) — I picked ranges that hit APAC afternoon / CET morning / early PDT:
- Option A: 2028-03-16 08:00 UTC (13:30 IST / 09:00 CET / 01:00 PDT)
- Option B: 2028-03-16 09:00 UTC (14:30 IST / 10:00 CET / 02:00 PDT)
- Option C: 2028-03-16 12:00 UTC (18:30 IST / 13:00 CET / 05:00 PDT)

I'll attach demo-utc-slots.ics with those three slots. If you'd rather we pick a single time and I create a Teams invite, say which option works and I'll lock it in.

Camila: looping you for ICS + Teams link if we lock.
Soojin: can you share the Chili Piper param that forces UTC? I know there's a query param we can append; don't want to guess.

Marcus — quick note on Chili Piper: you can append &force_timezone=UTC to the meeting URL (it is documented in our internal playbook). That forces the widget to render in UTC for all visitors. It isn't supported by every Calendly instance, though.

If we're short on time, I recommend sending an ICS and adding a short line in the body: "Canonical time: UTC — please accept the invite; local time conversions shown by your calendar are authoritative." That message avoids end-user confusion and prevents the widget from reinterpreting the chosen slot.

Also: when there's a CET/IST overlap, daylight saving changes in EU (Mar 26 this year) can shift local labels; using UTC sidesteps DST glitches entirely.
